blocks.title: Awareness Program Development, Execution, Reporting, and Monitoring comparison
Awareness Program Development, Execution, Reporting, and Monitoring exam shortcuts
items: Choosing topics, audience, goals, and metrics → DEVELOPMENT
Development happens before the program is delivered.
Example: Define phishing-training goals and target groups.
Training is being delivered to employees → EXECUTION
Execution means carrying out the plan.
First phishing simulation establishes click rate → INITIAL MONITORING
Example: First campaign shows a 22% click rate.
Compare phishing results every quarter → RECURRING MONITORING
Recurring measurements reveal trends and whether training is working.
Example: Click rate drops from 22% to 8% over several campaigns.
Awareness program should not be one-and-done → RECURRING
Security behavior and threats change, so training and measurement should continue.
Example: Repeat targeted training after new phishing trends appear.
blocks.example: First identify the human-security problem: phishing, suspicious behavior, user guidance, or awareness-program measurement.

questions.q: A security team chooses awareness topics, target audiences, goals, metrics, and delivery methods. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Program development defines what the awareness program will contain and how it will be measured.

questions.q: Annual security training is launched to all employees. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Execution means delivering the planned awareness activities.

questions.q: The first phishing simulation records a 22% click rate to establish a baseline. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Initial monitoring establishes the first baseline measurement.

questions.q: The organization compares phishing click rates every quarter to determine whether awareness is improving. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Recurring monitoring tracks awareness performance and trends over time.

questions.q: A phishing trend changes and the organization updates training content, then measures results over the next several campaigns. What principle does this demonstrate?
choices: Awareness should be continuous and recurring
Awareness is a one-time annual task
questions.explanation: Security awareness should adapt to evolving risks and be measured repeatedly.
